chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no wudu (ablution) due to madhy from desire, nor from arousal, nor from kissing, nor from touching the private part, nor from lying together; and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it.

key_terms.الثَّوْبُ: garment, which does not require washing from it
key_terms.الشَّهْوَةِ: desire or lust as a cause associated with the fluid
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution), whose obligation is negated here

ai.seo_question: Does madhy require wudu (ablution) or washing the clothes and body in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that madhy does not invalidate wudu (ablution) and does not require washing the body or clothing. It addresses common causes associated with its occurrence and clarifies that they do not entail ritual purification measures in this case.
